Messages.Body:
This is a report of both the draft tournament played last saturday,
and the Dutch ECQ and Open National Championships of yesterday.

SATURDAY: DRAFT

On saturday, only 6 players showed up for the 5 SW, 1 CE and 2 BH
boosters-draft. Judges Emile and Tobias decided to play to allow for 2
tables of 4, playing a 2R + F.

The final table was composed of Emile -> Tobias (me) -> Mark
Kolmershlag -> Peter Bouwman -> Paul Wiggers.

Mark had managed to draft a beast, and I had a fairly bad opening
crypt. I brought out Jacko and 2 small-cap !Brujah, but couldn't bring
out Rigby because Emile had already brought her out. I did manage a
non-bleed deal from Emile because I would otherwise contest Rigby with
him, leaving him in a bad spot against Paul.

Mark brought out Beast and back-rushed the weenies into torpor. After
a while, I managed to get out Jost (i think) and managed to oust Mark.
Emile couldn't convince the table I was the threat as I started to
work on Peter, but Peter wasn't going down fast enough, and my minions
went down to Emile, who bled me out. The game then timed out.

1. Emile, 1.5 VP
2. Tobias 1 VP
3-5 0,5 VP.

Decklists may be posted in this thread - I know I will post mine, as
soon as I retrieve my deck from where I left it.

SUNDAY: ECQ / Dutch National Championships CONSTRUCTED

After eliminating the mysterious double-counts in the Archon, 56
players were discovered to have shown up for the 1st Dutch ECQ/NC (43
of them had pre-registered). This made for 12 tables, so 2 extra
tables were moved into the location and the prelimenary round were
underway without any significant problems. In the prelimenary rounds,
26 GWs were earned out of a possible 36, with 9 tables timing out in
various rounds (of which 7 without GW).

After the first three rounds, the finalists were:

jo herroelen 2 GW 8.5 VP (!Tor CoT/Anthelios/Parthenon)
alexander schrijvers 2 GW 8 VP (Howler / Setites)
dieter arhweiler 2 GW 5.5 VP (Tor Bigcap Vote / TGB)
peter bouwman 1 GW 8 VP (Weenie aus w. concealed guns)
yuri nuyten 1 GW 6.5 VP (Xaviar)

Original seating:

Peter -> Jo -> Dieter -> Yuri-> Alexander

Alexander doesn't get a Howler until he's bought his 8th vampire, and
transfers no vampires before that (possibly afraid of Yuri's combat?).
Before howler gets a chance to act for the first time, she's hit by
Pentex Subversion. Ouch for Alexander.

1st tableswitch (by Dieter):

Peter -> Jo -> Dieter -> Alexander -> Yuri

Alexander and Yuriare ousted by Dieter with help from Jo after Jo's
proposed a 3-2 split in Dieter's favor.

2nd Tableswitch (by Dieter, made possible by master-cycling for TGB
with Jo's Anthelios)

Jo -> Peter -> Dieter

Dieter is at a ton of pool, Jo has very barely escaped with his life.
At this point the players look around, decide that #1 and #2 are
decided already anyway and that Peter deserves a 3rd place, so they
all withdraw.

A bizarre game, possibly again calling for some changes in the nature
of the game (I could explain, but you had to be there). Further
comments by the players/spectators in this thread are very welcome!!

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
I'll throw in my experience for the day.

I was playing a pretty standard !Tor bleed/untap/bloat deck relying
mainly on Jost and Gretha. Decklist is at the end of the post.

Table was: me -> aus/cel gun deck -> Tzimi eagle's sight block -> howler
setite bleed -> g1/2 Gangrel bigcaps

The first round started bad. I was seated first, and had three 6-caps
and a 4-cap in the Crypt (which is really bad for the deck since it
relies a lot on Enchant Kindred at superior). I did have the dreams in
hand, but it got suddended by my prey. I just settled for Jost in turn 3
which was a good choice in retrospect since everybody else started
getting a fattie as well, except my prey who brought out Remilaird in
turn 2. I brought out two more minions and did some art scams and
enchanted to the 4 cap with Jost. I also bled into my prey a bit. He
responded with totally walling up, not moving forward at all. The Setite
bled out the Gangrel deck in five or so turns. This looked bad. My prey
was playing mr. Wall, my predator has just gained 6 pool and all I could
do was sit and wait, simply by having a hand full of stuff I couldn't
play. I was lucky to draw into my single copy of specialization pretty
soon after that giving me some more options. All the while, the Tzim had
been silently building up, bleed-poking for one or two and happily
bloating with three Bdolls and a hunting ground. I exchanged some combat
with my predator (who was out of stealth), which got my minions really
low on blood. Both my predator and prey were *still* looking at my shiny
Sabbat Toreador (you know, I *hate* these people looking to the right
all the time). I pointed out that it was the Tzim that was the threat
and not me and lucky enough, they agreed. The three of us sealed a
two-turn non-agression pact in order to deal with the Tzim. This
basically meant I got to rebuild some, while they used resources to deal
with my (now former) cross-table buddy. After two turns, I sort-of
mentioned to my predator we should be careful not hurting the Tzim too
much, since he was quite low on pool. My prey took the bait and went
full-forward, thinking he had a chance to oust the Tzim. He almost
managed, but left him at four pool. That was my queu. I my own turn I
dropped the Palla Grande and bled through my prey with 4 bleeds for 3.
The Tzim was just in reach of a social-charm-palla grande-sheila mezarin
bleed, but he produced another wake. I got him the next turn and from
the on it was a mop-up. 4 point and a GW. Sure a good start for a
qualifier.

Round two sucked. Simple as that. I had a good crypt and a good hand.
But the seating was horrible. It was like this:

Me -> Cailean Wall -> Tremere bruise/bleed -> pre/vic/aus with
warghouls -> Anneke becomes Alastor

Yup, I was sitting between two blocky-combatty decks. As it turned out,
my prey blocked every action I ever took, be it undirected (art scam) or
directed (bleed for one to get the edge away from my grandprey),
triumphantly yelling "WELCOME TO THE WALL" every time he blocked me.
What a moron. Whatever he didn't block (like 3 actions the whole game)
was blocked by a 2nd tradition Anneke. Lucky for me, my grandpredator
played an Anarch Troublemaker pretty early on, making the Alastor deck a
non-threat, so I figured I'd settle for half a point. I got Parity
Shifted a few times, but I delayed one, and another one got DI'd and
from then on I made sure to stay low on pool. I almost managed to make a
deal for one point, but the table timed with only the Tremere having
gained a VP because of my prey's stupidity. Talk about people that only
look left...He didn't take a single action forward and didn't block like
15 equip actions because he feared a Burst of Sunlight.... When he *did*
move forward he got deflected thrice in a row, leading to the only oust
in the game. Oh and he also rushed Anson for no real good reason. There
was some good talking about votes all the while because nobody had vote
lock, making the game somewhat enjoyable, but it was clear there were a
couple of newer players at the table who didn't really watch table
balance and only wanted to survive. Oh well, it got me half a point.

In round three my 4-player-table curse caught up on me again, since I
have been seated at a 4player table in the last round of every
tournament I played. If I wanted a shot at the final, I needed to get 3
VP's at the very least. Seating:

Me -> Gangrel temptation -> ventrue vote/bleed/toolboxy -> Lucinde
Alastor vote

I didn't draw any 7-cap *again* in the crypt and my opening hand
consisted of 3 wakes and 4 masters. Great. Fucking great. I did have a
dreams again and since I was sitting 4th, I got out my 5 cap first.
Stupid mistake, since I should have waited a turn and get Jost out,
since he was the only guy with superior presence in the crypt.
Nonetheless, the dreams gave me some remarkable buildup speed, so I had
my whole crypt out in no time. I bled into my prey quite good, but him
having Nadima (+1 intercept) out and me having minions without superior
presence (majesty untap, which I need really bad) shut me down until I
drew into a Creepshow Casino. The game developed really really slow,
with some Parity shifts being thrown around and Horatio Ballard failing
to become prince 5 or 6 times. Anyway, I was doing bad. Really bad. I
had drawn nothing but reaction cards during the whole game and all my
Art Scams and bleed cards were somewhere down in the remaining 50 cards.
The table didn't have any really strong decks and I'm sure that if I had
drawn a normal selection of cards (and crypt!) I'd swept easily. But as
it was, I was just hunting, blood dolling and recovering from a Reins of
Power that hurt me for 4 and a KRC for 3 in the same turn until I could
get Greta Kircher out.
That's when the clock started ticking. With 20 minutes left, I was
looking at a good shot at a GW. I had convinced my grandprey it was a
good plan to oust my prey together and then I'd help him oust his prey
for the 2-2 split. Since he was at 5 pool it looked like a good idea,
but he couldn't know I had no intention (and no reason) to keep that
deal. So, he started mind numbing gangrels left and right, hit my prey
with some KRC, which finally gave me some room (did I mention he walled
up for no real good reason?) to move some cards. That's of course when
you draw a new dreams and get to move more cards than you really want
to, but to make a long stroy short, I hurt him. He, of course, responded
by walling up even more, empty his minions to survive, so I slowed down,
blocked and delayed my predator some more and I was basically in control
of the table. But that fucking clock.... I prepared my minions,
finetuned my hand, got rid of an Aranthebes and made sure my prey was
out of wakes. I had to move in and get that VP fast. Really fast. The
Palla Grande was sitting in my hand, I was pretty sure nobody had a
Sudden (my grandprey had been allowed to play Giant's Blood on a 1 blood
9-cap) and I was *sure* I could exactly kill my prey with my 5 minions.
My predators turn. He untaps. He thinks. Come on make it quick, boy,
we've got 5 minutes left and *I have this table*. Don't stall, I can
get you all, I want my final. He smiles.... and puts a Pentex Subversion
on Greta..... Fuck. Fuck...........

The table timed.

Afterwards, I complimented him on the Pentex. It was the exact right
card at the exact right minion at the exact right time. Well played, a
very close game. The clock got me. I knew I should have asked for extra
time when one of the players went to the bathroom :-). Oh well, 5 points
and a GW will have to do.

Thanks to the organizers for a great day of fun and the good new
location. I finished 14th (I think), enough to qualify, but I already
did that in Belgium. I'm still not sure if I'll make it to Heidelberg,
but we'll see.

Why is this particular deal supposed to be stopped? Could you include

have enforced?

I will tell you why I 'allowed' the deal to exist.

1. Since it's the finals, each player's goal is to get the highest
ranking. This depends on VPs taken at this final table, also taking
into account rank on entering the final.

2. Jo and Dieter have broken deals in the past (AFAIK). Therefore,
they have proved to be able to pursue a longer-term strategy
(including deal-break) while following a shorter-term strategy of
following the deal. (I am not sure how my decision would have been
modified by the hypothetical knowledge that, until that point, Jo and
Dieter had been pathological deal-keepers, but if that discussion is
of interest, I suggest we put it in a different thread.)

3. Dieter will get a GW if this deal is succesful, thus gaining first
rank, satisfying the ‘play to win' demands for him. Jo will gain 2VP
(behind Dieter (if the deal is kept)), thus gaining second place and a
chance to still take 1st place if Jo breaks his deal.

4. It is very likely Jo will die to Peter with 0 VP if the deal with
Dieter is not made. Even if Jo does not die, he is effectively put in
full defense mode, so his fallback-plan could only be to maximally
exploit holes in Dieter's defense if they occur (unlikely at that time
due to Dieter's pool amount, among other reasons), or hope for the
time-out to get a high finishing rank (determined by his #1 rank on
entering the final). A time-out without ousts by anyone was unlikely
at the time of the deal.
A counter-deal involving Jo and Peter, or Jo and other players at the
table, is unlikely to have been more beneficial to Jo than the deal
with Dieter. Furthermore, it wasn't proposed or discussed with any
seriousness. Having total information at that point (like the judge
could hope to achieve) might have changed that fact, but as a judge I
will not provide a player with an ‘out' based on the
information/experience I may have – I will block an illegal deal, but
I won't "play his deck for him".
I cannot spell out all the details of play and there's no videotape of
the final, but I hope you will accept my estimate of the state of
play. If you do not, we could collect evidence of the other
finalists/bystanders, but I believe this point will stand.

5. Thus, both Dieter and Jo are maximising their (expected) rank, by
my reasoning. Once the deal is made, I believe they are allowed to
fulfill it.

I am ready to stand corrected by valid arguments or examples, BTW. If
I was wrong, I will admit it and learn from it.

As to the call for change – if I was wrong, there are 2 possible
solutions: fix me, or fix the rules around the game to prevent me or
people like me from being wrong again. Fixing me is something I'll do
myself – fixing the rules around the game depends on your preference
for shoe-horning players and/or judges, and is something I would leave
to LSJ/the RT.

If I was right, your call for change may still be valid, but for
different reasons. (We could then also call it my call for change, as
I indicated by saying "possibly again calling for some changes in the
nature of the game" in my initial post of this thread.) While I am not
opposed to VP deals nor breaking them, I would prefer to see the
decision power of deals lowered as opposed to hard-fought play of
cards. This is a personal preference and (hopefully) has no impact on
how I judge games.

I do think I see a trend of finals (and games) increasingly decided
early by deals, but I've only been playing on a higher level for the
past 2 years, so my data is a bit short. Whether this is a phase, a
continuous trend, something cyclic – I don't know.

Nit-pick: at this tournament we had many players from The Netherlands,
Germany and Belgium, and a few from as far away as France. The result
could have as easily happened in some of these countries, I think
(although I have never played a tournament in France). I don't really
want to argue this point, though – it's just clarification.

My thoughts on Dieter breaking his deal: If Dieter had broken his deal
with Jo, this would have had some ‘scare' impact on the Dutch
(Benelux?) game. However, Dieter, while a very good player, is only
one of a number of very good players, who are unlikely to change an
effective strategy (table-dealing) in general – but they're likely to
change it to a large degree in the specific case of Dieter. Meaning

Hey there,
Finally found the time for it, as I knew our final game was going to

First of all however, thanks to Tobias and Emile for organising, and
most all players I met for a nice day of VTES!!
and off course, congrats to Dieter, but that he knows already

So, to explain what happened in the finals, I think a little
explanation about table seatingis is in order:

I went into the finals as highest ranked, so at the point where I have
to pick my seat it's setup as follows:
Dieter=>Yuri=>alexander=>? (sorry, can't remember for the devil of me)
I'd played Dieter earlier that day, and knew what he was playing. It
wouldn't have been so bad to have him as prey, providing my deck (I
was playing palla Grane/Foundation Exhibit Embrace) had the
opportunity to get going at least a little bit.
I knew what Alexander was playing, and definitely didn't want him as
pred or prey (pre/obf bleed, with howler and tons of steady intercept
on the table).
I was guessing Yuri was playing combat, so next to him wouldn't be a
good option either.
As it turns out, my pred was playing..AUS weenie :-((

So, during the game, most important factors IMHO were:
Alexander not influencing out a single vampire for zillion turns=>no
pressure whatsoever on my prey. Not even any necessity for him to even
think about maybe there being any actions from his pred he might want
to block..

Yuri influenced out Ramona, and after that Xaviar. 2 Vampires with no
inherent capability whatsoever to harm or even really hinder Dieter's
march foreward.

In no time, 5 (or was it 6) minions with concealed magnums at my preds
place, who still has not the least shimmer of pressure.

Ergo=>I can't get a single bloody Embrace into play, can't bloat,
can't even bleed my prey (Eagle sights, and nothing beter to do with
them).
Basically, we end up in a position where the only deck who can
actually do anything real to stop Dieter from a walk over (mine, under
normal circumstances)ends up at 6 pool, and no real way of getting out
of it.Basically, I will survive for maximum 2 more turns, tops.
On one side, I could use my remaining 2 turns (max) to really try and
do my very best to screw Dieter's game over big time (Fear of Mekhet
for Alexandra, Pentex Subversions, some Delays and DI's..all the
goodies in hand), to then just die 100% guaranteed, and virtually hand
the table over to my pred just before I get ousted..

Or, I can strike a deal with Dieter not to screw up his game and die
for sure afterward, but instead work together to make it a sure thing,
and come in second.

So, easy choice. With Dieter and myself working together with the
decks/positions as they were, it's a 200% guaranteed deal we set up.
And on top of that, even if Dieter breaks his deal and sweeps, it's
still ok, as nothing then changes the positions. The only danger would
be that Dieter breaks the deal which gurantees him the GW, and then
loses to the last player standing, the aus weenie.So that's not gonna
happen, as Dieter is an intelligent player.

Now, my personal view on the situation and what caused this deal: If
I'd have known what my pred was playing beforehand, with this deck I'd
never pick him for pred.I'd have probably seated myself in between
Yuri and Alexander.

Anyways, this dealing result is the +/- normal result of an AUS
weenie, and players intelligent enough not to suicide on it.
Such a deck will very often, providing it has more than 1 bright
player (not also playing intercept)at the table, or providing there is
no straightforward deck wellplaced (S&B as prey eg), force the table
into a deal.
Either you strike a deal with it, or you deal with someone else to not
be in the situation where they want you, which is: 3 player table
leftover, with 2 other players who have already overextended
themselves trying to oust the others. In that situation, vey few decks
still have what it takes to go by the weni.
In any case,this decktype profits tremendously from other players
trying to chew each other up, while they don't notice the threat the
weenie auspex poses..

Hence, I prefer to deal to consolidate 2nd place, over just getting
ousted after trying to chew up my prey.
Is that so strange?
I agree it doesn't make for very exciting play once the deal is struck
(it was more or less only a clean up action after that, rather than
surprising/exciting/original play),but I still don't see the issue
about dealing in a finals.
Personally,2nd place is not "first of the losers", it's "2nd out of 56
players while playing a deck I didn't even expect to get into the
finals with".
and I don't like screwing up other peoples play in a last attempt at
making myself seen anyway.
So, that's my idea. Think of it what you like..

Greetz
Jo

BTW: if anyone would ask me what I'd like to see changed i'd say:
forbid people to play auspex intercept weenie decks ;-)

A deal can be made at any time.
If the making the deal with the intention of honoring it is legal
within the play-to-win rules at the time it is made, then the
player is allowed to keep the deal when it comes time to do so,
even if breaking it would be better under the play-to-win rules.
If not, if making the deal is not "playing to win", then the
rules do not recognize the deal as an excuse to avoid "playing
to win" when the time comes to honor it -- that is, it must be
broken if honoring it at the time it comes to honor it is not
a "playing to win" move.

> And only if the chance of

This is a restatement of the set-up given above, yes.

> (still uncertain about
> what reasonable means exactly).

The judge's assessment.
It means that the judge doesn't have to factor in things like other players
saving you or making questionable plays when determining whether there's
"any chance" for you to make more VPs one way than another. The "what ifs"
only have to be considered if they are reasonable.

> If this deal is made, and found legal (or its legality is not
> questioned) then i am allowed to uphold the deal in a later stadium,
> even if breaking the deal at that point would win me the game.

Correct.

> If the deal is not found legal by the judge players can not make that
> deal.

It isn't that the player cannot make the deal. It is that the deal is
nothing more than table talk at that point -- the "illegal" deal has no
impact on how the "play to win" rule is used later.

> Now, what i gather from your responses here (and in the other thread
> you mentioned) is that you can make a deal regardless of the situation
> you are in, as long as you intend to break it. This means a judge is
> required twice during the deal-game. Once when the deal is made.
> (because if the situation stank for the player he is allowed to uphold
> the deal) and the second time when it comes to upholding the deal.
> because upholding a legally made deal can be illegal (because you
> intended to break it when making it).

The judge is required throughout the game, deals or no, but yes
(where "intend to break it" is replaced by "cannot honor it later
unless the activity used to honor it is legal in and of itself").

> Wouldn't it be simpler to just not allow a losing deal if the losing
> party could do better.

No, as that would then force the judge to give away privileged information
(i.e., information that one player knows and that the others do not).

> In other words without the option of the
> intention of dealbreak from the start.

> THUS that you can uphold your
> legally made deal, if you want. (and break it if you want).

You can do this already and still.

> Otherwise it would be so strange...
>
> judge: "you can make this deal, and it will be legal, but only if you
> don't uphold it"

That is not so strange. It is equivalent to:
The deal doesn't follow the play to win rules, so it (the deal) cannot
be used later to circumvent the play to win rules when the time comes
to honor it.
